title: outbox/queue.go
description: Migration(runtimeRole), the DDL text of the queue: the table stego_outbox.messages with the dispatch state, the attempt and conflict counts, the tenant, the outgoing key, the group of the state hook and a short failure code; row-level security enabled and forced with the tenant policy of the runtime role and the SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE policies of stego_outbox_relay; and the SECURITY DEFINER relay functions claim, move, release, purge_parked, purge_done, blocked and oldest, owned by stego_outbox_relay with search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp EXECUTE for the worker role only, never for the request-path runtime role, and a check of each argument: the claim limit 1 to 32, the lease 1 s to 5 min, a bounded delay and due time, an attempt change of -1, 0 or 1, a short failure code, no state for a token that is not the message's last claim, the tenant of the transaction when it is set, a release only in outcome unknown or reconciling, and no purge of a negative age or of a message enqueued as must land (column must_land). The migration makes the functions under SET ROLE stego_outbox_relay, refuses an owner that has no SET and INHERIT membership in that role, with an error that names the grant, and revokes the relay role's CREATE on the schema in the same text. They keep 'The queue is tenant-owned, and only the relay functions span tenants'. Queue.Enqueue writes in the caller's tenant transaction with the advisory lock of the tenant, destination and resource key, and sends a notice only for a declared live event source; it keeps 'A message is written only inside the caller's transaction'. Claim, Acknowledge, Retry, Blocked and the failure codes keep 'The queue keeps no error text, and the blocked view lists each stuck key once'. DeadLetters, the parked rows of one tenant, and the purge keep 'Purge removes only parked messages that may go'; purge_done keeps 'Done messages are purged after a bounded retention'. Enqueue sends the message identity alone as its notice. Options.PayloadLimits sets the payload limit of a destination up to MaxDestinationPayloadBytes (1 MiB), and PayloadLimit reads it; the table's payload check, named messages_payload_check, takes a jsonb text of 2 MiB and is made again on a table of an earlier migration. Re-review of PR #178: the payload column is bytea and holds the exact bytes that Enqueue checked; the migration makes an earlier jsonb column bytea, and changes the check only when pg_get_constraintdef differs, NOT VALID and then VALIDATE, under a lock timeout of 5 s; claim gives the payload as bytea. Final check of PR #178: the jsonb-to-bytea step refuses to run while an audit-sink message is open, seen with row-level security not forced for the owner in the migration's transaction.

title: outbox/worker.go
description: WorkerConfig, NewWorker, Run, StopClaiming and Finish: the claim under a lease, ordered delivery per key, retries, the bounded worker and its claim and work contexts keep 'One worker holds one message under a lease', 'Delivery is in order per key', 'A database failure is never a delivery' and 'Stopping the claims does not cancel a handler in flight'. The attempts limit, 25 by default and 1 to 1000, keeps 'The attempts limit is bounded, and a must-land message is never parked for a retry'. The purge timer and the retention keep their part of 'Done messages are purged after a bounded retention'. The instruments outbox.delivery.delay and outbox.oldest.age keep 'The delay from commit to delivery is measured per destination'. OldestAge reads the same relay function as the gauge and keeps 'The worker gives the oldest age of one destination'. Destination, Register and Registrations keep 'A destination is registered with its idempotency and its status lookup'. NewWorker refuses a pool with fewer than Concurrency + 2 connections. The metric outbox.hook.failures and the event outbox.hook_failed alert on a failed state hook.

title: outbox/events.go
description: Listener, the session interface that the source takes; Source, Subscribe for one tenant, Run, BadNotices, ReadFailures and Close: the bounded subscriptions, the live event source and its shutdown, where a lost session stops every subscription. A notice holds only the message identity; the source reads the message again under row-level security in a read-only transaction of each subscriber's tenant and passes the event only to the subscribers whose read finds the row; a notice that cannot be read is counted and skipped. They keep 'The worker and its subscriptions are bounded' and 'A live event is a hint for one tenant'.

title: outbox/dispatch.go
description: State, the seven dispatch states, and Transition keep 'A message moves only through the dispatch states'. NotSent, TransientRefusal, PermanentRefusal and Conflict mark a handler's error, and IsConflict and IsPermanent read the mark; the classification of an attempt keeps 'An outcome is unknown when the request may have reached the destination', and the recovery of a handler panic keeps 'A handler panic is an unknown outcome'. Each step runs in a transaction of the message's tenant, and the attempt count at the claim with its three takebacks keeps 'Each dispatch counts as an attempt at the claim'. The claim of an unknown outcome keeps 'An unknown outcome is claimed under a lease and holds back its key'. The step after an unknown outcome keeps 'An unknown outcome is sent again only to an idempotent destination, with the same key', 'Reconciling asks the destination's status lookup' (Lookup) and 'A message with no safe next step is parked with an alert'. The conflict backoff keeps 'A consumer conflict is dispatched again with backoff and is not an attempt'. StateHook and StateChange keep 'A destination can follow its messages' state in the same transaction'. Worker.Resolve keeps 'A person resolves a parked message' and, through the Decider port and the Auditor, 'Resolve decides the resolve permission itself'. The dispatch measures the lease on the local monotonic clock from the claim: it sends nothing when less than the attempt deadline and two statements are left, and bounds the handler's transaction by the lease. A state hook that fails or panics rolls its change back, is counted, and lets the message wait out a backoff.

title: outbox/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: pgconn/listen.go
description: Listen and Listener, the outbox Listener adapter over one direct pgx session: Listen takes a tenant.Config, makes the checks of tenant.Open with tenant.Connection before it connects (the pooler guard and the verified TLS transport check, with the loopback test mode), runs tenant.CheckSession on the session, and refuses a session whose startup process ID differs from pg_backend_pid(); Listener.Listen sends a notice with a random nonce after LISTEN and refuses the session when it does not come back. PID gives the server's process ID. They keep 'The listener session comes from the connector package'. The package doc says that pgconn is the one package of the runtime module that imports a driver.

title: controller/queue.go
description: The FIFO controller Run and the keyed queue: Source, Options, KeyedSource and KeySink, whose Add never waits and whose AddWait waits one caller at a time for a slot; RunKeyed, RunKeyedWithResult, RunKeyedWatch, RunKeyedWatches and their result forms; the capped backoff of keys and scans; the restart after a reconnect, which keeps due times, capacity and interrupted work; the collector, attached for the whole run; and the drain that runs the queued keys while the watch waits for its reconnect delay, takes no new key after it and lets running actions finish. It keeps 'Every item reaches its action unchanged, one key at a time', 'The queue is bounded with backpressure', 'A reconnect keeps the schedule', 'Backoff follows its cause' and 'Admission never blocks a producer'. While it drains, the queue lets workers take keys but does not report ready.

title: controller/scan.go
description: Scan and ScanFrom over cursor pages: opaque cursors of at most 1,024 bytes of UTF-8, a page size bound, a timeout for each page read and a page budget that returns progress; ScanStream with its open and receive timeouts and its item limit; and RunSweep with its groups, streams, workers and pass deadline. It keeps 'Scans resume after the last success with opaque cursors', 'A stream is bounded and closed', 'A sweep validates first and classifies each failure' and 'Scan progress is exact'.

title: controller/retry.go
description: The cycle: Checkpoint and ScanCheckpointed, RunObservation, which keeps time for the commit after the work, CycleState with EncodeCycle, DecodeCycle and ValidateCycleTransition, ScanCycle, ScanCycleWithOptions and ScanCycleParallel, and CycleRetryOptions, the retry policy of one action: at most four attempts, a delay from 1 ms to 1 s and not above the action timeout, and a fresh budget for each attempt. It keeps 'Retries are off by default, bounded, and retry only the action' and 'A retry never outruns its budget'.

title: controller/telemetry.go
description: The collector Metrics with its fixed Prometheus exposition and its cleanup sampler; Monitor, Process and the probe command; and Telemetry, the owner of the one provider set of the process, which the first user starts and the last user closes. Each operation is its own trace root with one completion log and one duration sample, and the instruments are the fixed stego.controller.* set. Providers is the provider set that it takes, which *otel.Runtime satisfies, and ServiceEvents sends service.failed through the probe runtime. It keeps 'Each operation is its own trace with a fixed outcome, and telemetry holds no private value', 'Overlapping controllers share one private provider set, and a failed callback emits one event', 'One collector per controller, fixed in size', 'The monitor serves metrics on loopback only, within fixed limits', 'Startup shares one telemetry runtime', 'Each operation logs once, at a severity its outcome sets', 'Cleanup sampling is its own bounded worker' and 'An operation root keeps its context and bounds its span'. Each operation span is a root that the telemetry runtime starts (StartOperation), with a name of SpanNames; without a collector, each completion log and each failure log is also one JSON line on standard error. The collector's QueueReady serves the readiness of the controller mode. It keeps 'Controller logs reach standard error when no collector is set'. Start fails when the runtime does not register a name of SpanNames. The standard error lines wait in a queue of LocalLogLimit lines with one writer: a line beyond it is dropped and counted, and the close drains the queue within the shutdown limit.

title: controller/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: otel/runtime.go
description: Providers, the export connection, its bounds and the trust file: New reads and checks the settings (an origin with no port gets port 443), opens the one verified TLS gRPC connection with no wait, starts the private tracer provider with the trace ID ratio sampler and the bounded span queue. The SDK span keeps no event and no link; a record of each recording span of the runtime keeps the name, the attributes and the failure mark that the runtime sets and the probe events that SpanEvent adds, at most 64, and the span is exported with these only, so code that holds the span cannot add data or a span of its own. Shutdown stops the providers by the earlier of the caller's deadline and three seconds, and Close wraps it. It gives the providers, the collector state, the service name, the instance identity and SpanEvent to the probe package, and keeps the traceparent rule and the export failure counters. New takes the closed set of operation span names; StartOperation starts an operation span of a registered name as a root or a child, with the fixed attributes stego.operation, stego.outcome and stego.retry, exported with its record only, and gives the Finish that sets the outcome and an error status with no message. It keeps 'A runtime package starts an operation span through the runtime'. The caller of StartOperation holds the span context only, a span that does nothing; without a provider the operation still gets IDs; Registered tells the registered names. SpanEvent takes the probe's key of internal/spanevent and plain names only, and at most SpanRecordLimit spans record at one time, the rest dropped and counted.

title: otel/http.go
description: The server span wrapper and request metrics for HTTP: Handler and Route, the final status observation, the route pattern set on the span's record, and the fixed request duration and active request instruments of HTTP and RPC. The health and discovery routes stay outside Handler on the service's top router.

title: otel/rpc.go
description: The RPC span and call metrics: TraceRPC, the seventeen gRPC status names set on the span's record, the six failure codes and the call duration record.

title: otel/logs.go
description: Completion logs and the private-data rules: the fixed event names, the severity of each outcome and the fields of one completion log per call. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 (ST-SUP-RP03-LC12): SetErrorCode gives the fixed error code of a denied or failed call to its completion log, as the attribute error.code; Handler and TraceRPC give each call a place for it, a code of another form than lower-case letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' is ignored, and the log of a call that passes holds no code.

title: otel/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: internal/spanevent/spanevent.go
description: Key, the capability to add a probe event to a span of the telemetry runtime, and New, which makes a key that is not zero. Only a package of github.com/jsell-rh/stego/registry/runtime can import it: the probe runtime makes its one key, and code of a service cannot add an event, a name or an attribute to a span of the runtime.

title: tenant/tenant.go
description: The Tenant type, with its one unexported field, and New, its one constructor, which takes a sealed Source: Claim of an Identity, which reads the tenant only through seal.TenantOf, or Requested with the action it serves and a Decision, which reads the allowed tenant and action only through seal.DecisionOf and accepts only that tenant and that action. ScanRows, the row reader, and the unexported column build the tenant of a column that a statement reads, the tenant list or a claimed outbox row. They keep 'A Tenant is never zero and comes only from its three sources, which the code holds by type'. WithTenant, FromContext and Middleware, which sets the tenant from the identity that the service's verifier returns, keep 'The context carries one tenant or fails'.

title: tenant/tx.go
description: Begin runs SELECT pg_catalog.set_config('app.tenant', $1, true) as the first statement of each transaction, and Commit commits only while the setting still holds the tenant and otherwise rolls back with ErrTenantChanged; they keep 'Every transaction starts with a transaction-local tenant setting and ends with it unchanged'. Querier gives a function the statements of the transaction and no commit. Config, Guard and checkConn keep 'The pooler guard refuses a session setting': Guard refuses a connection option, a startup parameter other than application_name and any after-connect statement, and checkConn refuses a connection that holds app.tenant outside a transaction. Guard checks a Config.Conn as it checks a DSN, and refuses a Config with both. Re-review of PR #178: Guard refuses a Conn with AfterConnect or AfterNetConnect, and works on a copy of it.

title: tenant/each.go
description: Each, Func, Failure and EachError keep 'A multi-tenant worker opens one transaction per tenant': one transaction for each tenant through Begin, the next tenant after a failure, the error of a canceled context in each failure it caused, and one error that names every failed tenant. EachListed runs Each over the tenant list.

title: tenant/owner.go
description: OpenOwner, the owner connector, opens only for MigrationJob; Open, the runtime connector, checks at startup that its role, also through a role it is a member of, owns no table, is not a superuser and holds no BYPASSRLS. Both run the pooler guard's check on each new connection and discard a connection that comes back to the pool with app.tenant set. Opened tells whether a pool is one that Open or OpenOwner returned and is not closed, from a weak set that they fill, so the command and query runtimes can refuse another pool. They keep 'The owner connector serves only the migration job' and 'A runtime can tell a pool that tenant.Open returned'. Config.Conn, the connection configuration of the PostgreSQL adapter's opener, is opened as it is (a copy), with no DSN parsed, and refused when it or a fallback does not verify TLS; Config.Pool sets the pool bounds (ST-SUP-RP04-LC09 on PR #177). Re-review of PR #178: Open checks verified TLS on its own copy of the configuration, which the pool then opens with. Connection gives that checked copy (Guard, then the transport check) and CheckSession the pooler guard's check of one session, so the listener of pgconn opens its session with the same checks (ST-SUP-RP01-LC20).

title: tenant/provision.go
description: Migration gives the SQL text of the table stego_tenants in a named schema, with a CHECK on the tenant ID, and of its two write functions, which have the search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, name the table with its schema and change only the tenant of the transaction. List reads the active tenants in tenant ID order; Provision and Retire, with their Hook list run in the same transaction, keep 'The tenant list is the tenants table that provisioning writes'. The text makes the table with IF NOT EXISTS and the functions with OR REPLACE, so it runs again on a database that it made (ST-SUP-Q97).

title: tenant/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: internal/seal/seal.go
description: The sealed interfaces Identity and Decision, each with only an unexported method that returns the mark, the marks IdentityMark (the tenant claim and whether it is present) and DecisionMark (the allowed tenant ID and the action, provision or retire), which only NewIdentityMark and NewDecisionMark make with data, and TenantOf and DecisionOf, which read the data of the mark and give no tenant for a zero mark, a nil value or a nil embedded value. They keep the seal of 'A Tenant is never zero and comes only from its three sources, which the code holds by type'.

title: pgconn/connect.go
description: Not written yet. The connector package github.com/jsell-rh/stego/registry/runtime/pgconn, the one package of the runtime module that imports a database driver (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R06): the tenant runtime's connector, which opens the pool with the session guard and the checks on each new and each returned connection. The code moves here from tenant/tx.go and tenant/owner.go; until it moves, tenant/tx.go keeps 'The pooler guard refuses a session setting', and this file takes that contract when the code lands.

title: audit/event.go
description: Event, with operation and hash_version, its enums, New, which sets hash_version 2, and Validate keep 'An audit event has a fixed shape, and its request fields are untrusted'. New and clean keep the cleaning of the untrusted values of 'Untrusted values are cleaned, states pass the redaction, and no value reaches an error'; State keeps its bytes unexported, so SetStates, the redacting path, is the only way to set the states. SetStates and Redact keep 'Redaction before storage: pii is redacted, secret is never stored' at any depth. Canonical, CanonicalRecord and Encode keep the encoding half of the hash contract, and their errors name the field and no value.

title: audit/chain.go
description: Hash, Link and ZeroHash, over the canonical record of the row's hash_version, keep 'The hash is SHA-256 over the canonical redacted record and prev_hash, in one chain per tenant'. Verify keeps 'The verifier walks one tenant's chain from its checkpoint and checks it against every anchor': it takes a tenant.Tenant and refuses the zero tenant before any statement, checks the latest retention checkpoint against the anchors at its seq and against the rows below it, streams the rows in seq order and keeps only the previous hash and the anchors. Anchor holds the tenant, the kind, the head and the count.

title: audit/patch.go
description: Diff, Apply and ParsePatch keep 'The patch is RFC 6902 over the redacted states': a pii field at any depth that changed gets a replace with the redaction marker, and a secret field is in no operation.

title: audit/record.go
description: Writer.Record keeps 'Record writes a transaction's events as one batch and takes the chain lock last' and the commit half of 'The audit row commits with the change, or alone with its outcome': it takes the tenant.Tenant of the caller's transaction, locks the tenant's chain head once, gives consecutive seq values and sets recorded_at from the database clock after the lock. RecordOutcome and RecordRead write in an own short transaction on the audit connections with tenant.Begin and tenant.Commit, always with a new ID; RecordRead fails at once with ErrReadAfterRecord for a request that already called Record, and FailedOutcomes counts the failed outcomes. Record also keeps the enqueue of 'Every audit row is enqueued for the sink, keyed by its id'. Tx is the part of *sql.Tx that the package uses (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R06); StatementError names the step and the SQLSTATE and no value. RecordRead takes no error code for a read that succeeded, with the outcome ok, and only the fixed code ErrorCodeUndecided, with the outcome failed, for a read that failed (ST-SUP-RP11-LC16). Record refuses with ErrTooLarge, before its first statement, an event whose sink message is above MaxSinkMessage (1 MiB) (ST-SUP-RP05-LC14).

title: audit/sink.go
description: The Sink interface keeps 'The sink is a port with no way back': Append(events) and Anchor(anchor) only. Destination.Deliver keeps the delivery half of 'Every audit row is enqueued for the sink, keyed by its id': it refuses a message that is not canonical or whose hash does not cover its event, and a duplicate event ID (ErrDuplicate) is a success. DeliverFor reads the payload back into its canonical form, since the outbox keeps it as jsonb, refuses with ErrBadMessage a message that it cannot read or that names another tenant than its outbox row, and gives the rest to the sink. Re-review of PR #178: DeliverFor reads the exact stored bytes, with no rewrite into a canonical form.

title: audit/jobs.go
description: Anchorer.Tick, LateAnchors, SkippedBoundaries and Health keep 'The anchor job anchors each tenant's chain at fixed boundaries under the fenced lease': one transaction per tenant with tenant.Begin and tenant.Commit, from the audit table, at the multiples of the period since the Unix epoch, with the boundary in audit_anchor_boundaries and lease.Held.Fence as the last statement; a miss clears only after the commit. DDL keeps 'The audit tables are partitioned, tenant-walled and append-only, and one owner function maintains them': the four tables with forced row-level security, the reject triggers, the boundary guard, the grants and the SECURITY DEFINER function audit_maintain() with search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, which also keeps 'A partition drop leaves a retention checkpoint of each chain' and restores the tenant setting. Maintainer.Run fences each call first under a lock timeout and again last, enqueues the retention anchors, commits with no tenant set, and its Health names a missing partition of the next month.

title: audit/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: audit/auditoutbox/auditoutbox.go
description: Queue and Sink keep 'The audit runtime gives the outbox adapter and the sink destination'. Queue is the audit.Enqueuer on the outbox queue: each sink message goes in the caller's *sql.Tx as a message of audit-sink, idempotent and must land, with the event ID as message ID and the key as outgoing key. Sink.Destination is the registration in the form of authz.Relay.Destination; Deliver parks a message that audit.Destination cannot read or that names another tenant, and retries a sink error. It is a package apart from audit because the outbox runtime's tests use the audit Writer. PayloadLimits gives the payload limit of audit-sink for the outbox queue, and NewQueue refuses a queue whose limit for audit-sink is below audit.MaxSinkMessage.

title: authz/port.go
description: The Decision and Relationships interfaces, Port, and the request and result types keep 'The decision port has the AuthZEN shape, and deny is a decision' and, with Write for one request of touches and deletes, 'The relationships port writes idempotently and returns the written-at token'; Consistency, Fresh and AtLeast keep 'The floor is at_least(token), and minimize-latency does not exist'; the opaque Token, ParseToken and PageToken keep 'A token is opaque, is stored per row, and is never compared'; ResourceID and NewResource, which build the tenant-qualified resource ID with the separator /, its reading back, the check of Port that refuses an evaluation of any other ID, and the search of Port, which is not exported so that only Handle.Search and the conformance suite reach it, keep 'A resource ID at the provider names its tenant'. PageToken.Provider names the provider of a page token, so the query runtime can store it in the text form of a cursor and make it again with NewPageToken (ST-SUP-RP11-LC15).

title: authz/spicedb.go
description: SpiceDB, the provider of both ports over gRPC, keeps 'The SpiceDB provider maps the port one to one', with Head for the floor, a ContextError for 'Caveat context is a map, and a missing field is an error', and the fixed error texts of 'A provider error carries fixed text and no subject or caveat value'.

title: authz/relay.go
description: Relay is the outbox destination authz: Deliver, Destination and Hook keep 'The relay is FIFO per resource key and parks a poison entry' with the outbox runtime, and 'A revocation's status is kept in its own record' through the state hook, which counts and alerts on a change the function does not count; the locked floor transaction, which writes the tuple and DefaultMarker in one request and keeps its written_at as the floor, Check, which refuses a schema with no marker, and TableFloor keep the floor of 'After a revocation lands, every check of the service is at least as fresh as its token'; Observe, Watch and ReadFailures keep 'A revocation that is not delivered in time raises an alert'; DefaultAlertBound and WithAlertBound keep 'The delivery alert bound defaults to 5 seconds and is positive'; Deliver, which parks a tuple whose resource, subject set or direct subject in the resource shape is not of the delivery's tenant, upgrades a payload of version 1 with the tenant of the outbox row, and stores the token on the row of the ID's key, keeps 'A resource ID at the provider names its tenant' for the relay; the floor marker, which holds no tenant data, keeps its fixed IDs.

title: authz/subject.go
description: Subject, SubjectOf, which builds the ID from the issuer and the subject, ServiceAccount, Principal, Person and System keep 'Every principal is a subject, and a service account is one too'; ServiceAccount, which refuses a name with a /, keeps the person and service account shapes apart from a resource ID for 'A resource ID at the provider names its tenant'; StagingPrincipal, which takes staging.Staging, keeps 'The staging principal of a consumed message comes from a sealed constructor'; Context, NewContext and ContextError keep 'Caveat context is a map, and a missing field is an error'.

title: authz/handle.go
description: Runtime, Bind and Handle with Evaluate, EvaluateBatch, Search, List, Relate and Unrelate keep 'The handle decides at the floor and declares relations only through the outbox' and 'The handle holds only its allowed relations and no provider'; Revocation and Wait keep 'A transaction's tuple writes are one revocation, complete only when the relay lands it'; Status keeps 'A revocation status is read only by the tenant and principal that made the write'; DecideTenant keeps 'The Decision that the tenant runtime takes comes only from this package'; Decide is the decision port of the outbox's Resolve; Migration keeps 'The migration keeps the runtime role out of the floor, the revocation counts and the outbox states', with authz_floor, the revocation records and the function authz_revocation_state, which the NOLOGIN role stego_outbox_relay owns; the handle's refusal of a resource ID, a subject set or a direct subject in the resource shape of another tenant, the search mapping with DroppedResults and the metric authz.search.dropped, Search, which fills its page from further provider pages within maxSearchCalls, and Decide, which sends the resource in the form of the message's tenant, keep 'A resource ID at the provider names its tenant'.

title: authz/conformance.go
description: Conform, Suite and Report keep 'Every provider passes the conformance suite', with the other-tenant case of 'A resource ID at the provider names its tenant': the suite refuses a grant without a tenant and expects a deny on the same key of another tenant.

title: authz/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: internal/staging/staging.go
description: Staging and NewStaging, the key of the staging principal and its one constructor, and Valid keep the key of 'The staging principal of a consumed message comes from a sealed constructor'; only the command runtime calls NewStaging, which TestStagingImporters checks.

title: idempotency/migration.go
description: Migration, the DDL text of idempotency_keys, keeps 'The key table is scoped by tenant, principal and key': the ten columns, a key of at most 255 characters, a status check of in_progress or completed, the primary key (tenant_id, principal_id, key), response_headers and response_body as bytea, and an index on expires_at for Purge. It also keeps 'The key table is tenant-owned, and only the purge function spans tenants': row-level security enabled and forced with the tenant policy on app.tenant; the purge function idempotency_keys_purge in the schema of the table, SECURITY DEFINER, owned by PurgeRole (stego_outbox_relay), with search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp, a cut-off held at the clock of the database and a limit of 1 to MaxPurgeBatch; the policies of PurgeRole for SELECT, DELETE and a lock-only UPDATE; no EXECUTE for PUBLIC. Each statement runs again with no error.

title: idempotency/wrap.go
description: Wrap keeps 'The key row is inserted first and completed in the same transaction', 'A duplicate in progress gets 409, a changed body 422, and a match a replay' and 'A transient failure stores nothing': it takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock with no wait on a hash of the tenant, the principal and the key mixed with the OID of the key table, inserts the key row with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING in the caller's transaction, runs the handler, and completes the row in the same transaction; otherwise it reads the row FOR UPDATE NOWAIT and answers 409, 422 or a replay. The headers are stored in a length-prefixed binary form, so every byte comes back. A lock failure, SQLSTATE 55P03 or a cancel in a statement of Wrap is 409, and any other database error is a StatementError that hides its SQLSTATE (ST-SUP-RP10-LC25). Tx (with Rollback, so only a transaction fits) and Row are the consumer-side interfaces, SQLTx adapts a *sql.Tx, and Wrap expects READ COMMITTED. KeyFrom reads the Idempotency-Key header as an RFC 9651 structured string and gives ErrKeyMissing or ErrKeyMalformed for the 400.

title: idempotency/fingerprint.go
description: Fingerprint and Canonical keep 'The fingerprint is SHA-256 over method, path and canonical body': canonical JSON has sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace, one escape form for strings and one exact decimal form for numbers. Derive keeps 'An outgoing key derives from the inbound key with its scope, the destination and the effect'. Each hash is over parts that each have a 4-byte big-endian length prefix. FieldFingerprint keeps 'A fingerprint over a declared list of body fields': it keeps the named top-level members of the JSON object body and returns the fingerprint over the method, the path without its query and the canonical kept body. Re-review of PR #178: an object that repeats a key, or holds two keys equal under simple case folding (foldKey), is refused by Canonical, Fingerprint and FieldFingerprint.

title: idempotency/purge.go
description: Purge keeps 'Purge is a bounded batched delete at 24 hours': it deletes expired rows in calls of the purge function idempotency_keys_purge, each one DELETE of at most the batch size (default 1000, at most MaxPurgeBatch), with a pause between batches (default 100 ms), and DefaultRetention is 24 hours. Querier is the database it takes, which *sql.DB satisfies.

title: idempotency/conformance.go
description: Conform keeps 'The conformance tests cover replay, reuse, race and crash': it runs the four cases against a Subject, which is the store's own functions that send a request through its wrapped write and count its key rows, and returns each case that fails with the reason.

title: idempotency/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: idempotency/purgejob.go
description: NewPurgeJob and PurgeJob keep 'The runtime gives a purge job that runs on a declared interval': Run runs one Purge each time the interval, 1 minute by default, passes on its clock, until its context ends; a mutex keeps two purges from running at once; Runs, Failures, Deleted and Health report the runs, and a failed run does not stop the next. Re-review of PR #178: the first purge runs at start, the pause of a purge waits on the job's clock and ends with the context, and a purge that the context ended is not counted. NewPurgeJob refuses a batch above MaxPurgeBatch.

title: money/money.go
description: Currency, Parse, Money, New and Of, Add and Sub keep 'Money is int64 minor units with a currency, and adds only within one currency': an int64 amount of minor units with an ISO 4217 code from list one (case-sensitive), Add and Sub that refuse two currencies with an error that names both and refuse an overflow with ErrOverflow, and no float in any exported signature. Allocate keeps 'Allocation loses no minor unit': whole shares rounded toward zero in 128-bit arithmetic, then one minor unit at a time to the largest fractional shares, ties to the lower index; it refuses an empty, all-zero or negative ratio set and a ratio total over 64 bits. The code table and Currency.Exponent keep 'Each currency has its minor-unit exponent, and test and metal codes are refused': each accepted code has its ISO 4217 exponent, and every code whose minor unit ISO 4217 gives as N.A. (XXX, XTS, the metals, the bond units, XDR, XSU, XUA) is refused.

title: ledger/transfer.go
description: Post and Pend call ledger_post and ledger_pend, PostPending and Void call ledger_post_pending and ledger_void, and Reverse calls ledger_reverse: one statement each, after Go refuses an entry set that does not balance, another currency, bad text and a transaction that is not READ COMMITTED. They keep 'A transfer is written by one owner function call that must balance and keep the limit', 'A pending transfer is immutable, and it is posted or voided once' with the state machine transition and its errors ErrAlreadyPosted, ErrAlreadyVoided, ErrExpired and ErrExceedsPending, 'A retried transfer returns the original, and a reused key with another body is refused' with ErrKeyReused and IDs in lower case, 'A reversal is a new transfer that names the original, at most once', and 'A ledger call refuses an isolation that can overdraw' with ErrIsolation. New refuses a dollar sign in a ledger ID or account code and a close date in the future. Open calls ledger_open with the account ID and its declared code, and returns ErrAccountExists for an ID that exists. stateError maps the SQLSTATE of each refusal of an owner function to the error of the package.

title: ledger/balance.go
description: Balance and BalanceAt keep 'A balance derives from entries after the latest snapshot, on the account's normal side'. Balance calls ledger_balance, the one derivation that the limit also uses: the latest snapshot plus the posted entries whose transaction ID is at or above its through_xid, each signed by the account's normal side. BalanceAt sums the posted entries by effective_at. Sums are numeric in the database and an int64 overflow is an error.

title: ledger/jobs.go
description: Jobs, Snapshot, Check, Sweep, Health and Components keep 'The snapshot and check jobs run under the lease, and a failed check is a health signal' and 'An expiry sweep voids each expired hold'. Each job works only while the process holds the controller lease, and runs each tenant's transaction within a budget of half the renew slack and before the lease deadline, with a lock_timeout and a statement_timeout, fenced with lease.Held.Fence and committed with tenant.Commit. Snapshot calls ledger_snapshot with the fencing token. Check runs as REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY and is incremental: through ledger_check_sums it reads only the entries from the last checked position, each once, finds each ledger that does not sum to zero and each newer snapshot that differs from its predecessor plus the entries between them, keeps the position before a failure, and reports each pending transfer not voided one Period after its expiry as a failure of the sweep; Health then reports unhealthy with a reason that names ledger_check. Sweep voids each expired hold through Void with the key expire:<ID> (SweepKey). Components gives the three jobs for the controller mode only, each every Period.

title: ledger/guard.go
description: DDL keeps 'The ledger tables are written only by owner functions, and the guards refuse every change'. The text creates accounts, transfers, entries and balance_snapshots, tenant-owned with forced row-level security and balance_snapshots with no foreign key to accounts; statement triggers that refuse entries that do not balance or are not inserted with their transfer; the guard trigger BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE (and TRUNCATE) on transfers, entries and accounts, which lets through only the one change of status from pending and the one reversed_by that the owner functions make, each checked at commit against the new row that names it; and the owner functions ledger_open, ledger_post, ledger_pend, ledger_post_pending, ledger_void, ledger_reverse and ledger_snapshot, SECURITY DEFINER with search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, which check the tenant, READ COMMITTED and each argument, read the declared currency, close date, pending timeout, snapshot interval and account codes from the text, and enforce the balance, the accounts, the currency, the limit under the row lock with open holds by the clock after the lock, the split of a post, the mirror of a reversal with no other key, the expiry by the clock after the lock and the body fingerprint, and compute each snapshot. The runtime role gets SELECT only on the four tables and EXECUTE on the owner functions and on the read functions ledger_balance and ledger_check_sums.

title: money/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: ledger/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: modes/modes.go
description: Parse, Selection and Registry keep 'A mode is a named component set, selected by a repeatable flag with all as the default'. Parse reads the --mode option, which can occur more than once, or else the comma-separated STEGO_MODE, uses all when there is neither, and refuses an unknown mode. Register and Start run only the component set that the generated code registered for each mode.

title: modes/shutdown.go
description: Readiness keeps 'Each mode has its own readiness'. Ready and Check answer for each mode, Listener makes the api mode ready while the server accepts, Watch adds a backfill whose stall makes the controller mode not ready, and Handler serves /readyz and /livez. Sequencer keeps 'Each mode shuts down in its own order'. Run waits on the signal channel that the generated code gives, and Shutdown fails readiness first and then runs the api, worker and controller sequences of the selected modes. WatchQueue adds a controller queue, such as *controller.Metrics, that must run and be ready for the controller mode to be ready. With no watched queue the controller mode is never ready.

title: lease/lease.go
description: LeasesTable is the table of the leases, and Declare adds the row of a lease name. New, Acquire and Renew keep 'A lease is one row; Acquire and Renew are two UPDATEs that increment the token': Acquire runs its own statement, and Renew runs its own statement with the token the holder holds, so a renew after an expiry, a takeover or a release takes nothing. The defaults are 15 s, 10 s and 2 s. Fence and WithToken keep 'Every write under the lease carries the fencing token and fails on a higher one'. Hold keeps 'A holder that cannot renew stops before the lease expires' and stops on the fenced error. Release makes the lease expire.

title: lease/backfill.go
description: BackfillsTable is the table of the checkpoints. The fenced checkpoint statement keeps 'The checkpoint row carries the fencing token and refuses a lower one'. Run and its batches keep 'A backfill batch is one short transaction', with the key stored with its type (integer, uuid, text or composite, a composite as typed, length-prefixed parts) and given to the step in that type; 'The backfill resumes from its checkpoint and marks completion' and 'A new fill value starts a repair pass'. The Observer calls keep 'Backfill progress goes through the probe as counts'. Stalled and the stall watcher keep 'A stalled backfill fails readiness, never liveness'. Flush writes the last checkpoint again at shutdown, before the lease is released.

title: modes/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: lease/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: lease/periodic.go
description: Job, NewPeriodic and Periodic keep 'A periodic job runs in controller mode at its declared interval': Run, the run function of the controller mode's component periodic-jobs, runs each job at start and then each time its interval has passed since its last run, only while the controller lease is held and with a context that ends when the lease stops; a failed or panicking run is counted, reported by Health and does not stop later runs, and a due run with no lease is skipped. It is in the lease package because modes and lease are one runtime package and the tests of each import the other. Review of PR #178: the interval runs from the start of one run to the start of the next, a run's context has the lease's expiry as its deadline, and after a skip the job tries again at the retry period (PeriodicConfig.Retry, DefaultRetry by default). Re-review of PR #178: a run's context ends when the lease's expiry passes on the lease's clock, read again after each renew (Held.watch), in place of a deadline read at start.

title: command/handle.go
description: Handle, Repo, Repository, Entity, EntitySpec, List, ListSpec and Loaded keep 'The handle is bound to one transaction, tenant and principal', 'No raw database connection is reachable through the handle', 'Every read and write runs in the bound transaction with the tenant set', 'The handle gives the fill its command's or worker's probe', 'Each entity value through the command handle is a loaded value', 'A locked read holds its row until the transaction ends', 'A locked list is bounded and locks only allowed rows in key order' and 'A write through the handle carries the version of its loaded value'. The generated code gives the statements of each entity, with the tenant as $1; the handle runs them in the bound transaction, decides a read before it locks, takes each lock in a savepoint that it rolls back for a row that a second decision denies, sets lock_timeout before each lock and write, decides a malformed key, which the entity's generated ValidID refuses, as a missing row, refuses a delete of a GetForUpdate value, and keeps one state for each attempt that closes when the fill returns and that keeps the first conflict or internal error. A command's locked read (GetForUpdate, GetForDelete, ListForUpdate), its update and its delete also decide the command's permission on the row, and its create under a parent decides it on the parent (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05). Re-review of PR #178: EntitySpec.Parent ties a create's parent to the new row (checkParent); an entity registers with one runtime only (register). Final check of PR #178: a child entity (Parent and no resource type) takes the decision of its parent: GetForUpdate, GetForDelete, ListForUpdate, Update and Delete take the parent's loaded value (decideParents), and an update that moves the row takes both parents. Re-check of PR #178: decideMove makes an update of any entity with a Parent that moves the row take the new parent's loaded value and decide on it. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05): EntitySpec.Parent is a list of Reference values, each with the referenced entity, its resource type, the reader of its ID, the declared permission and the relation; a create decides the declared permission of each set reference on its loaded row and writes its relation through the authorization handle, an optional reference that is not set is not decided, and a move decides on the new referenced row and moves the relation.

title: command/authz.go
description: Authz, the handle's authorization part, keeps 'The handle decides through the authorization handle at the floor': its evaluations go through the authorization runtime's handle of the same transaction, on a loaded value of the handle. The decisions of the repository keep 'The command's permission covers its declared writes' (a command makes no decision per write) and 'A read through the command handle is authorized and audited as a query read'; for a worker and a consumer they keep the decisions of 'A worker handle decides on each resource it touches, and a consumer decides as both principals'. Every resource that it decides on is built with authz.NewResource, so its ID at the provider is qualified by the tenant (ST-SUP-RP06-LC22). decideCommandOn decides the command's permission on a row; decideWrite calls it for a command's write and for the parent of a create, and a deny is not found (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05). Re-review of PR #178: Relate and Unrelate take the loaded value of the tuple's resource, refuse a tuple of another resource, and decide the command's permission, or the worker's, on it.

title: command/audit.go
description: Each event carries the command or worker name as operation. The audit buffer keeps 'Each write through the handle is audited in the transaction, as one batch at the end': each write buffers its event, redacted by field sensitivity, and the attempt records them with one call of Record just before COMMIT. auditRead writes the audit row of each read of an entity with a pii field on the audit connections. RecordOutcome writes an outcome row and logs and counts a failure, and ErrorCode gives the fixed code of an error of Run. checkAuditPool keeps 'Read audit rows have connections of their own'.

title: command/effects.go
description: Effects and Destination keep 'Effects leave only through the outbox' and 'A staged effect carries a key scoped to its tenant, principal, destination, effect and entity': Stage refuses authz, audit-sink and an undeclared destination, derives the outgoing key with idempotency.Derive over the inbound key and the entity's ID, refuses a second effect of one name for one entity, and the attempt enqueues the staged messages in one batch after the fill. Re-review of PR #178: in a command, Stage decides the command's permission on an entity with a resource type, and needs a locked or written value of any other entity (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05). Final check of PR #178: an effect for a child row takes the parent's loaded value and decides on it. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 (ST-SUP-RP10-LC07): Destination.Effects holds the declared effect names, and a command's Stage refuses any other name and breaks the call.

title: command/run.go
description: Runtime, New, Command and Run keep 'Only the generated code ends the transaction', 'The handle is invalid once the fill returns', 'Run calls the fill inside the idempotency wrapper', 'A panic in the fill rolls back everything', 'A conflict runs the fill again only as the command declares', 'A lock wait ends before the request deadline as a conflict' and 'The command runtime commits and opens its pool only through the tenant runtime'. Each attempt opens tenant.Begin, sets lock_timeout before the key insert and before each statement of the wrapper, decodes a copy of the body again, and commits with tenant.Commit; COMMIT errors are a conflict, an internal error or an outcome that is not known. New takes only pools for which tenant.Opened reports true. A COMMIT error that tenant.Commit marks as not committed is a conflict or an internal error. The fill runs on a goroutine of its own, so runtime.Goexit counts as a panic; an attempt that did not commit clears its audit read mark (Writer.Forget). CommandSpec.Permission and Resource and Request.Resource keep 'Run decides the command's permission on its resource before the fill': after the authorization bind and before the idempotency wrapper, each attempt reads the resource row's token in its transaction and decides the permission at the floor; a deny, a missing row and an ID that is not a key give ErrDenied, with no fill call and no key row. Review of PR #178: Config.Entities are the entities that FromRequest takes, and New sets the slot seal; the token statement of a Resource must take exactly $1 and $2 and lock the row FOR SHARE or FOR KEY SHARE; the decision uses the floor only, so an existing and a missing row get one consistency; the attempt's state carries the command's permission. Re-review of PR #178: the token statement, with its comments removed, must be one SELECT that ends FOR SHARE; New registers each of Config.Entities with this runtime only. Final check of PR #178: the token statement matches one strict form, with no quote, comment, parenthesis, WITH, TABLE or VALUES. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11: a command with an empty key runs without the idempotency wrapper and leaves no key row (ST-SUP-RP10-LC11); Resource.Service names the service-level resource on which a create of an entity with no parent is decided, with no row read (ST-SUP-RP10-LC31); the handle is bound with the relations of the written entities' references, which only the runtime writes.

title: command/worker.go
description: RunWorker and RunConsumer, which bind the command handle to a worker's service account, keep the worker contracts of the command runtime (ST-SUP-RP10-LC16 to ST-SUP-RP10-LC22, ST-SUP-RP10-LC26): the service-account binding, the decisions on each resource, the tick transaction and its effect key, the once-per-message consumer, the fencing of a run under a lease, its deadline before the lease can expire, and a conflict that waits for the next run. RunWorker opens its own transaction with tenant.Begin, not tenant.Each, because lease.Held.Fence needs the *sql.Tx that a tenant.Querier hides; RunConsumer runs in the outbox worker's transaction of the message's tenant, sets on_behalf_of of its audit rows to the staging principal, and parks a message whose staging principal is denied or whose fill returns a declared refusal (Refusal). RunWorker returns an outcome of COMMIT that is not known as it is. Refused marks an error as a declared refusal; a *Refusal of serve.go is one with no mark.

title: command/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: internal/loaded/loaded.go
description: Value, the loaded value that the command handle and the query handle share, with its one constructor New and the readers Of and Fields, which only packages of the runtime module can call. It keeps 'Each entity value through the command handle is a loaded value': Value has no exported field, so the generated loaded type, a pointer to it, has no composite literal and no conversion; its Value method returns a deep copy through the entity's generated Clone; and one type serves both handles, so a generated probe method takes the loaded value of either (ST-SUP-RC34-OC01).

title: command/slot.go
description: SlotKey and FromRequest keep 'Slot code makes a loaded value from a validated request'. FromRequest makes the loaded value of an entity from a deep copy of the request entity; it takes the key that SlotKey gives, whose type is not exported, so only generated code that holds the runtime can call it and a fill cannot call it in a way that compiles. The value names no row and no handle state, so no handle takes it for a write, an effect or a decision. Review of PR #178: a key works only from a runtime that New made, and FromRequest takes only an entity of Config.Entities (ErrNotRegistered).

title: command/serve.go
description: ServeSpec, Serve, ServeRPC, Refusal, NewRefusal, RPCCode, SetPath, NewID, ValidUUID, Must, ClonePointer, StateOf and EqualPointer keep 'The command runtime serves a command over HTTP and gRPC' (ST-SUP-RP10-LC33): the steps of a command handler that are the same for every command, so the generated code passes only the ServeSpec of each command. Serve and ServeRPC bind the verified tenant and principal, read the idempotency key (required only when the declaration requires it), decode the request message, call Run, answer ErrDenied with 404 denied, a declared refusal of the spec, known by identity, with its status and code, a conflict with 409 conflict and an outcome that is not known or any other error with 500 internal, write the outcome audit row of a denied or failed command in its own short transaction, give the fixed code to the completion log (otel.SetErrorCode), and write a problem body or a gRPC status that holds the fixed code only. A *Refusal is a declared refusal that RunConsumer parks. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 (ST-SUP-Q74). BindIdentity, Bound, OutcomeOf, Outcome and RecordFailure keep 'The command runtime exports the bind, the outcome map and the outcome row of a request' (ST-SUP-RP10-LC34): Serve and ServeRPC use them, and so does a handler that decodes its own body.

title: query/handle.go
description: Handle, Spec, Entity, Row, Loaded, Repo and Repository.Get. bind binds the handle to one READ ONLY transaction, tenant and principal, which it shows for reading only, and refuses a transaction that is not READ ONLY or not READ COMMITTED. Repo gives only the repositories of the entities that the query declares it reads. Get reads with the tenant predicate in the bound transaction and decides the read at the floor also when no row exists: on the stored key of a row, on the fill's key and a zero token otherwise; a deny and a missing row are both not found, and a provider failure is ErrUndecided either way. Loaded has no exported field and no exported constructor, a copy of a loaded value is refused, and Value builds a deep copy from the stored row each time. Probe gives the query's typed probe. It keeps 'The query handle is bound to one read-only transaction, tenant and principal', 'No raw database connection is reachable through the query handle', 'Every read runs in the bound transaction with the tenant set', 'The query handle can write nothing', 'The handle gives the fill its query's probe' and 'Each entity value through the query handle is a loaded value'. A Get of personal data whose decision fails writes its read audit row with the code undecided before it returns ErrUndecided (ST-SUP-RP11-LC16). Row.Int32, Row.Float, Row.Bytes and Row.JSON read the column kinds that a generated load reads (ST-SUP-RP11-LC17).

title: query/authz.go
description: Authz, the authorization part of the handle, which decides only through the authorization runtime's handle of the same transaction, on a loaded value with its stored row token, and has no bypass and no relationship write; allowRead, the read decision of Get and Send; and Repository.List, which reads at most ScanLimit rows in one call, in chunks of at least MinChunk, from the first row with no key predicate, filters each chunk with one batch evaluation and returns a cursor at the last key it read, or uses the provider's resource search for an entity with a small expected cardinality, on the query's or the entity's list permission at the floor of each page. Every resource it passes the authorization handle has the tenant-qualified ID that authz.NewResource builds, and a search page reads its rows by SearchResult.Keys (ST-SUP-RP06-LC22). It keeps 'The query handle decides through the authorization handle at the floor', 'A read of a protected resource needs an allow' and 'A list through the query handle holds only allowed rows'. A page of personal data whose batch decision fails writes a failed read audit row with the code undecided for each row it read (ST-SUP-RP11-LC16). A list page whose batch decision or resource search fails gives ErrUndecided, which Serve answers with 503. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 (ST-SUP-RP11-LC18): ListRequest.Order orders a list by declared fields, each ascending or descending, with NULL values last and the key as the last tie-breaker; it reads the table in that order, refuses an undeclared field before any statement, and the cursor holds the order and the position of each order field.

title: query/run.go
description: Config, New, Runtime, Query, NewListQuery, Bound and Run. New takes only pools that tenant.Open returned. Run opens a READ ONLY transaction at READ COMMITTED with tenant.Begin, builds the typed probe on the call's probe, binds the handle, calls the fill once on a goroutine of its own, closes the handle and the probe as soon as the fill returns, panics or leaves through runtime.Goexit, in a deferred end that always runs, writes one read audit row, with the query name as operation, per resource of an entity with a pii field on the audit connections before the value reaches the fill, gives no result when the fill fails, panics or an audit write fails, and commits only with tenant.Commit. It keeps 'A read of personal data is audited per resource with the action read', 'The query handle is invalid once the fill returns', 'A failed or panicking fill returns no result' and 'The query runtime commits and opens its pool only through the tenant runtime'. Config.CursorKey is the key of the cursor MAC, of at least 32 bytes. auditedFailure writes the read audit row of a read of personal data that failed, with the outcome failed, the fixed error code and no state, and keeps 'A read audit row carries the outcome's error code'. Re-review of PR #178: a cursor key needs the service name, which is associated data of each cursor.

title: query/stream.go
description: Stream, Send and RunStream. Send takes only a loaded value of the stream's entity that this handle loaded, decides the entity's read permission at the floor at the time of the send through the bound transaction, sends on an allow, drops and counts on a deny, and sends nothing once the stream or the fill ended. The count of dropped messages never reaches the client. It keeps 'A streamed query sends only allowed loaded values, each decided at the floor'.

title: query/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: query/cursor.go
description: CursorText and ParseCursor keep 'A cursor has an opaque text form bound to its query': the text is the position of a table page or the provider's page token of a search, with an HMAC-SHA256 of the runtime's cursor key over the position, the query name, the tenant and the principal, in base64url. ParseCursor refuses with ErrBadCursor a text that was changed, does not decode or another query, tenant or principal got, before any row is read. Review of PR #178: the position is sealed with AES-256-GCM under a key that HKDF-SHA256 derives from the cursor key, with a random nonce and the service, the query name, the tenant and the principal as associated data, so the text shows nothing of the position. A cursor of a list in order holds, sealed, the order, the position of each order field with its type and the key (ST-SUP-RP11-LC18).

title: query/http.go
description: HTTP and Serve keep 'The query runtime serves a query over HTTP': the generated code gives only the query, Bind, Decode, the fill, Next and Encode; Serve reads the cursor parameter with ParseCursor before any transaction, runs the query with Run, writes the JSON response with 200, and maps a bad cursor or request to 400, a failed bind to 401, not found and deny to 404, an undecided read to 503 and any other error to 500, each as a problem response with a fixed title and no row data. Review of PR #178: Serve limits the body to MaxRequestBody with http.MaxBytesReader and sets Cache-Control: no-store on every response. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 (ST-SUP-Q84, ST-SUP-Q81): HTTP.Refusal is the refusal lookup; Serve answers a refusal that it knows with its status and code, every other error of 500 with the code internal, and gives the code to the completion log through otel.SetErrorCode. Refusal, NewRefusal and Lookup are the refusal type; BindContext and BindHTTP bind the verified identity to the tenant, the principal and the probe call; Limit and EncodePage are the list helper, and EncodeValue writes a get response.

title: query/rpc.go
description: RPC, ServeRPC, StreamRPC, ServeStream and BindRPC keep 'The query runtime serves a query over gRPC': the generated code gives the query, Bind, Decode, the fill, Next, Encode and the refusal lookup of the query's HTTP handler and the constructor of the response message; ServeRPC binds, reads the list cursor of the request message with ParseCursor, runs the query with Run and reads the JSON body into the response message with protojson; ServeStream binds, decodes and runs the generated Stream function, and sends each allowed value as a stream message. rpcError maps each error to a gRPC status whose message is a fixed code, as Serve maps it to a problem response, and gives the code to the completion log.

title: probe/probe.go
description: Declare, the observation descriptor and its checks, Call and Probe: Bind binds a call to the span of the context, the tenant, the principal's opaque ID and the operation, and reads nothing else from the context; Emit takes the descriptor and typed values only, checks them against the declaration, and holds at most 64 emissions until Commit or Rollback; after Returned, Commit, Rollback or Close each emission is dropped and counted; Muted is the probe of another emitter. It keeps 'A probe takes no free-text message', 'A probe is bound to its call and goes quiet once the fill returns' and 'A log record carries opaque correlation only'. Commit and Rollback end the call's child span, after its events, with the outcome committed or rolled_back.

title: probe/otlp.go
description: The OTLP sink: it takes the logger and the meter of the telemetry runtime and makes no provider, exporter or connection; an event becomes one log record domain.<name> with no body and, on a recording span of the telemetry runtime, one span event through SpanEvent, and an event that the span has no room for is counted as an otlp drop; a counter and a histogram become one metric with the fixed boundaries of their unit; the counters domain.probe.dropped and domain.probe.failed are labelled by sink only. It keeps 'An event becomes a log record and a span event', 'A counter or histogram becomes a metric', 'A span event and a metric carry no tenant or principal', 'The probe uses the telemetry runtime's providers only' and 'A domain histogram has fixed boundaries and cumulative temporality'. It holds the span event key of internal/spanevent, which only the probe makes.

title: probe/sink.go
description: Runtime, Start and Close: Start reads STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE and starts the OTLP sink only when the telemetry runtime has a collector endpoint; each sink takes records through its own queue of at most 1,024 that drops and counts; the end of a call sends each record under a recover that counts a drop; Close drains the console and OTLP queues, sends telemetry.runtime.stopped and shuts the telemetry runtime down inside one shared shutdown limit; Delivery reads the drop and failure counts. It keeps 'OTLP is on when a collector endpoint is set', 'The console sink is off unless the environment turns it on', 'No fill or declaration chooses a sink', 'Emitting never blocks, fails or panics the fill', 'Drops and write failures are counted', 'Emissions wait for the call's outcome' and 'Shutdown drains the console queue inside the shared budget'. Bind starts the call's own child span through the telemetry runtime's operation span when the span of the context is sampled and the runtime registered CallSpanName; SpanNames gives that name. Start fails when the telemetry runtime does not register CallSpanName. The generated code ends every call with defer call.Rollback() after Bind.

title: probe/console.go
description: The console sink: one JSON object or logfmt line for each record, in one write to standard output, with the timestamp, the severity, the service name, the instance identity, the event name, stego.outcome, the value, the correlation and the declared fields under fields; the built-in service and worker events have their own queue of 64, so a full queue of declared observations does not drop them, and are always one JSON line with no tenant, principal or operation; after the drain it writes telemetry.runtime.stopped. It opens no connection. It keeps 'The console sink writes one line per emission to standard output', 'The console sink opens no connection' and 'Built-in service events are always on the console'.

title: probe/values.go
description: Value and its constructors Text, Integer, Bool, Enum, Measure and Number, the check of a value against its field, and the text cleaning: a text value is cut to 256 bytes first, without the bytes of a split rune, then invalid UTF-8 and NUL become U+FFFD and the text is cut again on a rune boundary. It keeps 'A probe carries no private value'.

title: probe/recorder.go
description: Recorder, the sink in memory for fill tests: Bind, All, Emissions, ExpectEmitted and ExpectNotEmitted, which name the observation and list what was recorded; it keeps every emission in call order under a lock and drops none. It keeps 'The recorder captures every emission in order' and 'A fill test asserts an emission by name and fields'.

title: probe/builtin.go
description: The built-in observations with their fixed names and severities: Service for the six service events of the telemetry runtime, Worker for worker.run.failed, worker.tick.skipped and worker.tenant.unreached, Backfill for the schema backfill observations (it is the lease runtime's Observer), and NewBuiltins, which keeps the declared workers and the open schema changes, at most 127 each. Declare refuses their names. It keeps 'Built-in service events go through the probe' and 'Schema backfill observations are built in'.

title: probe/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: authn/verify.go
description: Settings, New and Verifier.Verify, with the token checks: the size of the token and its characters (the base64url alphabet and dots only), one JSON object for the header and for the payload with no duplicate member, at most 32 levels of nesting and no unpaired surrogate escape, the header with an alg of the declared algorithms of the allow list RS256 and ES256, the default RS256 alone, typ JWT, no crit, jku, jwk or x5u member and an optional kid, the signature with the exact key, whose one algorithm must be the token's (RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 for RS256, r and s of 64 bytes for ES256), then the issuer, an aud of strings only, the subject from the configured subject claim, the issue time, the expiry (refused at exactly exp) and not-before claims with the clock skew. Settings also carry the attribute claims, the bare-token opt-in and the problem type base and code prefix. ErrDenied, ErrSettings and the fixed refusal texts hold no token, claim, key ID or source detail. They keep 'No claim is given before every check passes', 'The declared algorithms of the allow list RS256 and ES256 only, each with its own key type', 'An ES256 key is a P-256 point, and its signature is r and s', 'Trust settings are explicit at construction', 'Oversize, ambiguous and invalid tokens are refused', 'Errors and telemetry hold no token, claim or provider detail' and 'The verifier is safe for concurrent use'.

title: authn/identity.go
description: Identity, which holds its tenant claim in the seal mark that seal.NewIdentityMark makes and has only getters, Principal, and the claim mapping: the dotted claim paths, the role reader (an absent role claim gives no roles), the tenant reader and the profile reader (preferred_username, email, given_name, family_name and the configured attributes), each from its configured path only, with the bounds and the clean text rule. They keep 'The verified identity is the only Identity, and it is sealed', 'Claims map to the principal, the roles and the tenant from configured paths only' and 'The Identity carries the profile claims'.

title: authn/keys.go
description: KeySet, KeySource, ParseKeys and NewKeySet: the key document reader by exact member names with its bounds (64 KiB, 32 keys, one key ID each, RSA keys of 2048 to 8192 bits with the exponent 65537, P-256 keys of 32-byte coordinates on the curve, each with its one algorithm), the PEM key file source for tokens with no kid, read once at start, the exact key ID lookup with no fallback, the issuer source, whose key document URL the discovery document gives once at start, the remote source over verified TLS 1.2 or later with no redirect and no proxy and a CA file that adds to the system roots, the file source, one load at a time, the cooldown of 30 s, a stale cache that answers a known key ID at once and starts one refresh, the outage window of 15 minutes, Stop and the refresh span with only the source kind and the outcome. They keep 'The RSA key size is bounded', 'One exact key ID, no fallback, and bounded key documents', 'The remote key source uses verified TLS with no redirect and no proxy', 'An unknown key ID refreshes the cache under a rate limit', 'A bounded outage window, and a removed key stops at once', 'Stop closes the verifier, and a zero value fails closed' and 'A PEM public key file is a key source, for tokens with no key ID'. The issuer source and the P-256 keys also keep 'An issuer is found through its discovery document, read once at start' and 'An ES256 key is a P-256 point, and its signature is r and s'.

title: authn/middleware.go
description: Verifier.Middleware, Verifier.Authenticate and FromContext: exactly one Bearer credential from the configured header, or a bare token when the declaration opts that header in, the verified Identity in the context under an unexported key only after Verify passes, the same credential rules for Authenticate, and the 401 answer with Cache-Control no-store, an RFC 6750 WWW-Authenticate challenge and the problem document with the declared type and code, the fixed detail, the instance and the timestamp, with no token. They keep 'The bearer middleware takes exactly one credential and denies safely', 'The 401 body is the service's problem document' and 'Authenticate verifies a credential for the shared-context transports'.

title: authn/authntest/server.go
description: The test key server (NewServer and NewServerAt, with its own certificate authority, on 127.0.0.1, stopped by t.Cleanup, with the discovery document of any issuer path (Issuer, SetDiscovery, RedirectDiscovery, Discoveries), Publish, SetDocument, Fail, Redirect, Hang, Delay and CAFile) and the token minter (Mint, which signs the header and claims a test gives with RS256, PS256, ES256, HS256 or none, also when they are not valid, with Key, ECKey, Claims, Header, HeaderOf, Document, Discovery and RSAJWK). They keep 'authntest serves a local key document and mints test tokens'.

title: authn/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: authn/discovery.go
description: The discovery URL of an issuer and the one load of its discovery document at start: the document bounds and JSON rules of a key document, the issuer member equal to the issuer, the jwks_uri member an HTTPS URL, fixed refusals that name the discovery document and are ErrDiscovery and ErrKeys, and the span authn.keys.discover with the outcome only. They keep 'An issuer is found through its discovery document, read once at start'.

title: service/doc.go
description: The package doc: it states the concern of the package and that the package is a library, not a framework (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01). It declares nothing and keeps no contract.

title: service/settings.go
description: The fixed setting names, Auth, SpiceDB, Settings, MigrationSettings, ReadSettings and ReadMigrationSettings keep 'Settings come from the process environment by fixed names': each setting is read by its fixed name or its file form, a connection string file is a safe regular file at an absolute path, a verifier setting that the declaration states wins and the environment may only match it, a SpiceDB address goes without TLS only to a loopback address, the cursor key holds at least query.MinCursorKey bytes, and a missing or malformed setting is refused with an error that names the setting and not its value. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 (ST-SUP-Q90). Auth also states discovery, the CA file, the algorithms and the subject claim of oidc-auth; with discovery no key document setting may be set, and STEGO_AUTHN_CA_FILE adds certificate authorities for a key URL or the discovery (ST-SUP-RC37).

title: service/service.go
description: Parts, Service, New and DialSpiceDB keep 'New wires the runtimes of a service from its settings': New opens the main pool and the audit pool through tenant.Open with the adapter's connection configuration (Parts.TenantConfig), connects to SpiceDB with the preshared key and refuses to start when its health check does not serve, starts the telemetry and the probes, and gives the verifier, the authorization runtime, the audit writer, the outbox queue, a command runtime for the declared commands and one for the collection commands, and the query runtime; a failed step closes what New opened. Only names and the constructors of the service's component packages come from the generated code (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05). The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 (ST-SUP-Q90). Parts.Workers holds the parts of the worker and controller modes, which Start takes (ST-SUP-RP14-LC04). New makes the key set of a declared issuer from its discovery document with the CA file, and StartStage names the stage of a start that a key source refused (ST-SUP-RP14-LC05).

title: service/migrate.go
description: Migration, Migrate, StepError and Stage keep 'Migrate runs the migration job in one fixed order': Migrate opens the database through tenant.OpenOwner and runs every step on one connection, as the owner role and with a time limit, in the order of the contract: the read-only ledger check, WriteSchema, the ledger of the adapter, the outbox, audit, idempotency and authorization migrations, the grants of the runtime role, the audit partitions and WriteSchema again; it stops at the first step that fails with a StepError that names the step, and Stage gives the stage migrate.<step> with no error text. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 (ST-SUP-Q90). The audit step also makes the lease table and the row of the controller lease stego.controller, with SELECT and UPDATE for the runtime role (ST-SUP-RP14-LC04). The tables step runs the migration text of the tenant list (tenant.Migration) in Migration.TenantSchema, public when it is empty, as the owner role after the ledger (ST-SUP-Q97).

title: service/workers.go
description: WorkerSettings, ReadWorkerSettings, WorkerParts, StartConfig, Workers, Start and Shutdown keep 'Start runs the workers of the selected modes, and Shutdown stops them once': Start opens the worker and relay pools through tenant.Open, builds the outbox worker with the parts' destinations, the relay and its watch for the worker mode, holds the controller lease stego.controller and runs the audit anchor job and the maintenance loop as periodic jobs of the lease runtime for the controller mode, and registers them on the modes registry; Ready and Handler answer each selected mode and name each stopped component; Shutdown runs the shutdown sequencer of the modes runtime once, releases the lease and closes the pools. The generated code passes only the constructors of its component packages and the declared values (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05).
